theory: A citeable paper is an immutable, versioned record of bytes actually acquired and read, separate from a search lead. A guarded library admits sources, one bibliography writer assigns durable citation identities, and statement inventory supports provenance-bearing assumptions without turning reading into proof.
instead_of: Let the model supply bibliographic metadata or cite a mutable search result; that would make references untraceable to what the session actually held.

absorption.rationale: Additional archives, queries, and statement inventory operations fit the current model, but a non-arXiv source requires a new identity model because stored records and library paths are keyed by versioned ArxivId.

world_mapping.rationale: Search leads, pinned records, archive manifests, bibliography entries, and assumption statements have distinct ownership and evidence roles.

abstraction.rationale: Acquisition uses an injected transport, clock, and library; archive admission is independent of arXiv metadata; bibliography writes are centralized.

justification.rationale: The code explains why bare identifiers must be resolved before admission, why records are rechecked on read, and why a bibliography is reopened under a lock for each modification.

honest_limits.rationale: Archive admission expressly disclaims sandboxing; search results are expressly not admitted records, and digests attest held bytes rather than mathematical truth.

rehearsals.requirement: Apply a stricter download and extraction quota.
rehearsals.why: Archive Limits and client timeout/interval inputs express these bounded acquisition policies.

rehearsals.requirement: Cite the same paper from two sessions without losing either update.
rehearsals.why: Bibliography is read per operation and owns its lock and sole cite path.

rehearsals.requirement: Admit a versioned publisher or DOI-only source that has no arXiv identifier.
rehearsals.why: PaperRecord, parse_id, and library path selection encode arXiv identity, so a generic source identity needs deliberate introduction.
